# Microsoft Teams fixtures: real structure, fictional content

Written by `make_fixtures.mjs` (run it to regenerate). People, ids, tenants, texts and links are invented. The structure (field names, nesting, nulls, `@odata.*` keys, id and time formats, body markup, file layouts) follows Microsoft's published example responses and the documented output of open-source exporters. Message ids are epoch milliseconds that match `createdDateTime`, as in real data. Tests: `test/importers-a/teams-real.test.js`.

| Folder | What it reproduces | Source of the structure |
|---|---|---|
| `graph-me/` | A delegated dump. `chats.json` is a `/me/chats?$expand=members` page (`#chats(members())`, `aadUserConversationMember` with base64 `id`, `roles`, `visibleHistoryStartDateTime` `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, `viewpoint`, `onlineMeetingInfo`). `messages/<chat>.json` holds message pages: a group chat as an **array of two pages** (`@odata.count`, `@odata.nextLink`), a 1:1 chat (`19:<guid>_<guid>@unq.gbl.spaces`), and a meeting chat as a **delta page** (`#Collection(microsoft.graph.chatMessage)`, `@odata.deltaLink`). The messages cover `systemEventMessage` and `unknownFutureValue` events with `from: null` and `<systemEventMessage/>` (membersAdded, chatRenamed, callStarted, callEnded); a deleted message (`deletedDateTime`, empty body); an edited one; `<at id>` user mentions and an "everyone" (`conversationIdentityType: chat`) mention; `<emoji>`; a `reference` file attachment; an adaptive card from a bot (`applicationIdentityType: bot`); a reply with quote (`messageReference`, content as a JSON string); a `forwardedMessageReference`; Unicode and legacy reactions with `displayName: null`; `messageHistory`; a `federatedUser` from another tenant; and an `anonymousGuest` with a 32-hex id. | Graph v1.0 docs: chat-list-messages, chat-list, chat-list-members, chatmessage-delta, chatmessage-replywithquote, concepts/system-messages, concepts/teams-messaging-overview, the chatMessage / chatMessageMention / chatMessageReaction / chatMessageAttachment resources |
| `graph-channel/` | `channels.json` from GET /teams/{id}/channels: `membershipType` `standard` and `private`, **no `@odata.context`** as in the docs' example. Channel messages fetched with **`$expand=replies`**: roots carry `replies@odata.count` and nested `replies`, `subject: ""`, and `webUrl` with `parentMessageId`. Also channel and team mentions, and a `/messages('{id}')/replies` page saved as its own file. | Graph v1.0 docs: channel-list, channel-list-messages, chatmessage-list-replies, chatmessage-post (beta: channel and team mentions) |
| `graph-getall/` | Teams Export API pages from two custodians (`/users/{id}/chats/getAllMessages`): `#Collection(chatMessage)` context, `@odata.type` on each item, the same messages in both files, and a 1:1 chat in which only one side wrote. | Graph v1.0 docs: chats-getallmessages; learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/export-teams-content |
| `graph-minimal/` | A trimmed page with only `id`, `createdDateTime`, `from.user`, `body`. The chat is named only in `@odata.context`. | https://github.com/jbelanger/export-teams-conversations (`samples/sample_teams_messages.json`; structure only) |
| `graph-per-message/` | One file per message: `archive/data/<chatId with : and @ replaced by _>.json` (the chat with `$expand=members,lastMessagePreview`), plus `archive/data/<chat>/msg_<id>.json`, hosted images and `archive/html/`. | https://github.com/codeforkjeff/teams-chats-export (`teams_chats_export.py`) |
| `graph-powershell/` | `teamschatsYYYYMMDD.json` and `mychatsYYYYMMDD.json` from `Get-MgBetaChat -ExpandProperty members` and `Get-MgBetaChatMessage` piped to `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 100`. Properties are PascalCase, and derived-type fields (`userId`, `email`, `@odata.type`) sit in `AdditionalProperties`. **Inferred** from the SDK model, not seen in a real dump. The Windows PowerShell 5.1 variant (UTF-16 with BOM, numeric enums, `/Date(ms)/`) is built in memory by the test. | https://github.com/kkgthb/powershell-ms-teams-chat-backup (`Get-Chats.ps1`) |
| `free/messages.json` | The Teams Free (personal) export, same schema as the Skype export. `userId`, `exportDate` without seconds, `conversations[]` with `threadProperties.members` as a **JSON string** (and as `[{MemberMri}]` in one chat), `threadProperties: null` for 1:1 chats, and `messages: null` beside `MessageList`. Conversation types are `8:` 1:1, `19:...@thread.skype` and `@thread.v2` groups, a `28:` bot, `48:calllogs` and `48:notes`. Message types are `RichText`, `Text`, `RichText/Html`, `RichText/Media_GenericFile` (`<URIObject>`), `Event/Call` (`<partlist>`), `ThreadActivity/AddMember`, `TopicUpdate` and `MemberJoined` (JSON body), and `Poll`. The markup covers `<quote author messageid><legacyquote>`, `<at id="8:...">`, `<ss type>`, `properties.edittime` / `deletetime` / `emotions` (an array, and as a JSON string), a sender given as a contacts URL, and the owner's empty `displayName`. The test wraps it in a `.tar` named `8_live_<account>_export.tar` with `media/` and `skype-parser/index.html`. | support.microsoft.com "Export or delete your data in Microsoft Teams free"; https://github.com/suurjaak/Skyperious (`src/skyperious/live.py`, `skypedata.py`); https://github.com/m00291/skype-parser; https://github.com/opravdin/skype-export-viewer; https://github.com/laxmikanth538/teams-parser |
| `purview-new/` | An eDiscovery (new experience) process report folder: `Items_<timestamp>.csv` with **display-name** headers (`Conversation ID`, `Conversation type`, `Item class`, `Message kind`, `File class`, `Channel Name`), CRLF line ends, two custodian copies of one transcript, a channel transcript (`Conversation name` = `<Team>,<Channel>`), and an email item (`IPM.Note`). Also `Summary_<timestamp>.csv`. **The exact header row and column order are not published**; field names and values follow the docs. | learn.microsoft.com/purview: edisc-ref-document-metadata-fields, edisc-review-set-teams-data, edisc-process-report-use, edisc-search-export |

The older fixtures in `../graph`, `../free` and `../purview` keep the CamelCase Items.csv header (`ConversationId`, `FileClass`, ...) from the review-set documentation.

Graph doc sources were read from https://github.com/microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-docs-contrib (`api-reference/v1.0/api/*.md`, `concepts/*.md`), which is what learn.microsoft.com renders.
